issues.acceptance: A representative native-renderer before/after capture reports raw frame times, one-percent low, hitch count, CPU/GPU attribution, and named script hot paths with 3, 5, 10, and 18 active enemies. Enemy separation is computed once from a cached stable roster per physics cycle, QA instrumentation performs no per-frame deep state snapshot or scene-wide scan in ordinary play, and AI behavior/spacing remains unchanged. llvmpipe evidence is recorded only as collector evidence.
issues.actual: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.
issues.expected: Ordinary gameplay performs bounded enemy steering and lightweight production work per frame; deep QA snapshots run only on demand or at a bounded debug sampling cadence.

blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Produce a loop-88 plan with exactly three independent task families: animation motion quality, protected feedback plus combat audio/VFX, and FPS combat AI, preserving clean boot, accepted deployment flow, retained weapon/viewmodel profile, authored map, and the protected tester_feedback presentation-only fixture contract.

diagnosis.root_cause: Loop 87 leaves three separate combat-readability surfaces: rifle animation remains a source/binding defect, the feedback fixture issue must now be handled as a protected verification-first presentation-only contract, and FPS combat AI must advance independently from animation and fixture work. The audio/VFX lighting increment belongs with feedback, but must be proven through ordinary or authoritative combat branches rather than by converting protected stems into combat truth.

stop_conditions: Do not modify candidate files, run-owned evidence, frozen context, issue ledger, or ignored Godot import/cache paths from this planner role.

Do not convert protected tester_feedback stems into authoritative combat outcomes, fabricate CombatFeedbackMatrix rows from those stems, or mutate active_latest/gameplay authority during isolated fixture verification.
Do not schedule deferred issues fp.qa.performance-runtime-unqualified, fps.weapon.report-audio-long-source, or fp.performance.runtime-hotpath-stutter as current-loop task issues.
Do not split, surgically edit, or per-bone compensate imported animation sources, retained viewmodel components, or authored map children.

strategy.rationale: Use the exact host grouping: animation motion quality as its own issue repair, feedback as protected fixture verification plus audio/VFX increment, and FPS combat AI as the separate player-visible combat increment. This avoids repeating rifle transform tuning and avoids weakening the protected presentation-only fixture policy.

code: Run Godot import and clean boot; reject editor/runtime script errors after deployment, firing, impacts, enemy hits, kills, protected feedback fixtures, checkpoint restore, Replay, and F6 reset.
Source-inspect tester_* actions for release-build guards and no physical release bindings.
Confirm retained AK-74M viewmodel source audio, component transform/profile, authored map instance, environment tuple, and accepted title-to-gameplay flow are preserved.
runtime: Start from fresh title/loadout/briefing deployment and prove gameplay input, captured mouse yaw/pitch, movement, ADS, fire, reload, pause/resume, F6, checkpoint restore, and Replay smoke before fixtures.
For animation, run tester_encounter_bravo_prepare and tester_encounter_charlie_prepare, then sample living actor clip/socket/muzzle/root telemetry and adjacent rendered frames.

For protected feedback, run tester_feedback prepare/advance/reset and verify receipts, owner identity, cleanup, presentation_only=true, authoritative_calls=[], and unchanged active_latest/gameplay authority.

For FPS combat and audio/VFX, run one ordinary or authoritative branch combat sequence with three visible enemy-to-player hits, one blocked-shot negative control, one player hit on an enemy, and one lethal enemy elimination.
visual: Capture shipped first-person screenshots for ordinary combat, Bravo prepared actor, Charlie prepared actor, enemy fire/player damage, material impact, character hit, and kill feed states.

Compare HUD and feedback to the PRD visual reference: transparent tactical hierarchy, top-left minimap, top-center countdown/compass, top-right restrained combat feed, lower-left vitals, lower-right weapon state, readable red damage pressure, and no broad opaque debug panels.
Use adjacent-frame captures for fire, reload, hit reaction, death, muzzle/impact VFX, and short feedback transitions, each paired with runtime state or game-time step.

Activated or prepared Bravo and Charlie living rifle actors expose truthful telemetry for weapon_family, clip source, genuine authored rifle status, socket binding, hand contact, muzzle direction, grounded root, and semantic state across idle or movement, aim, fire, reload, hurt, and death samples.

If a coherent licensed rifle-ready authored set is available, it is bound through the existing humanoid actor wrapper without source surgery and sampled living actors report genuine authored rifle semantics.

If no coherent rifle-ready source is available, Developer preserves or restores the last visually accepted component baseline as an interim regression repair, records missing rifle-source evidence, and does not claim issue closure.
